newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president attacks Pyongyang's "barbarism".
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president attacks Pyongyang's "barbarism".

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam condemned North Korea's submarine incursion as an "act of barbarism" on Thursday, while police stepped up protection of key facilities and national figures.
Kim's comments follow a warning by Pyongyang on Wednesday of "serious consequences" over the deaths of 22 North Koreans who came ashore from the submarine two weeks ago.

"North Korea's grave acts of armed provocation against the South, such as the recent infiltration of armed guerrillas into the South on a submarine, are unpardonable acts of barbarism," Kim said in a speech on National Foundation Day.
He said North Korea was "on the brink of an economic debacle but still caught up by an illusion that they can unify the Korean peninsula under communism".
Pyongyang's latest threat over the submarine was made at a border meeting with the U.S.-led United Nations Command, which monitors a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
A U.N. Command statement said a Korean People's Army officer had warned "that serious consequences, which would be announced, would occur as a result of the deaths of their soldiers".

That warning, plus an earlier threat to retaliate "a hundredfold or a thousandfold", has created such alarm that when a South Korean diplomat was bludgeoned to death in the Russian Far East city of Vladivostok on Tuesday the media immediately pointed accusing fingers at Pyongyang.
Hours later, tension was fuelled by reports that a South Korean businessman was shot and critically wounded in Cambodia.
Police were ordered to step up security around major facilities, foreign diplomatic missions and families of key figures against possible North Korean terrorist attacks, a Seoul police officer said.
"We are beefing up security and patrol duties to protect key government and social figures and their family members as well as major facilities across the country," he said.
South Korea has warned that the submarine incursion was a prelude to wider military action.
President Kim on Wednesday ordered Defence Minister Lee Yang-ho to ensure the armed forces were fully prepared to deal with any North Korean provocation.
A presidential spokesman said the latest North Korean threat was particularly serious since it was "so direct".
Pyongyang says the vessel was on a training mission and drifted into Southern waters after developing engine trouble. It has demanded the return of the vessel and crew.

A Seoul government official said the slain diplomat, Choi Duck-keun, was responsible for setting up escape channels for North Koreans fleeing through the Russian Far East, where several thousand work as loggers.
He was the first Seoul diplomat to be killed while on overseas duty.

The English-language Korea Times newspaper quoted an unnamed official as saying "South Korean officials engaging in North Korean refugee affairs have been constantly threatened by North Korean agents".
